rituals.name: Aashirbaad
rituals.significance: Elders of the other family formally bless the bride or groom, accepting them into the family.

rituals.name: Dodhi Mangal

items.item: water from a pond or river if the family follows that custom

rituals.significance: A last light meal before the bride and groom fast for the rest of the wedding day.

rituals.name: Gaye Holud

items.item: gift trays (tattva) sent from the groom's family
a yellow saree for the bride

rituals.significance: Turmeric touched to the groom is carried to the bride, linking the two families before the wedding.

rituals.name: Shankha Porana
participants: married women of the bride's family

items.item: a small bowl of water or milk

rituals.significance: The bride wears the white and red bangles that traditionally mark a married Bengali woman.

rituals.name: Bor Boron
participants: bride's mother and married women of the bride's family
rituals.significance: The bride's family welcomes the groom and his party at the wedding venue.

rituals.name: Saat Paak and Shubho Drishti

items.item: Wooden seat (piri) to carry the bride

rituals.significance: The bride, carried on a piri, circles the groom seven times, then lowers the betel leaves for their first formal look.

rituals.name: Mala Badal
participants: family members who lift the bride

items.item: Two flower garlands (often rajanigandha or marigold)

rituals.significance: The couple exchange garlands, traditionally three times, as a sign of mutual acceptance.

rituals.name: Sampradan
participants: bride's father or another elder who gives her away
rituals.significance: An elder of the bride's family formally entrusts her to the groom with mantras.

rituals.name: Yagna and Anjali
rituals.significance: The couple make offerings into the sacred fire, with the bride's brother passing the puffed rice.

rituals.name: Saptapadi and Sindoor Daan

items.item: a new saree or veil (lojjabostro) to cover the bride's head
seven betel leaves or small stones for the steps

rituals.significance: The couple take seven steps together; the groom then applies sindoor to the bride's hair parting.

rituals.name: Bashor Raat
participants: cousins and friends from both families

items.item: A decorated room with mattresses and bolsters

rituals.significance: The couple stay up through the night with younger family members, with songs, games and teasing.

rituals.name: Bidaai and Kanakanjali

items.item: A handful of rice and coins

rituals.significance: Leaving home, the bride throws rice over her shoulder to her mother, wishing prosperity for the home she leaves.

rituals.name: Bou Boron
participants: groom's mother and married women of his family

items.item: Plate of alta (red dye) and milk to step into

rituals.significance: The groom's mother welcomes the bride, who steps into the home leaving red footprints for good fortune.

rituals.name: Bou Bhaat

items.item: plate of rice and a new saree for the groom to give the bride

rituals.significance: The groom promises to provide food and clothing; the bride serves rice to the family for the first time.
